candidates.explanation: After verifying the reset hash, resetPassword only sets the new password and updates the user. It never revokes the user's existing sessions, for example with sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id }). The refresh endpoint (AuthService.refreshToken) only checks that the session exists and the hash matches. A device that was already signed in therefore keeps its valid session and can keep renewing its login after the reset. By contrast, AuthService.update calls deleteByUserIdWithExclude when the password changes.

fix.description: In resetPassword, after `await this.usersService.update(user.id, user);`, call `await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id });` to revoke all sessions.
